title: CM3419 2a Cassava (Lakan 2 (UPL Cv 6)): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: CM3419 2a Cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: CM3419 2a cassava is a cassava variety. 28.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others. Free guide.
excerpt: CM3419 2a is a registered cassava variety, also sold or known as Lakan 2 (UPL Cv 6) or Lakan 2. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Cv 11. Its record notes 28.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Lakan 2 (UPL Cv 6) or Lakan 2, this is the same cassava. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 28.8 t/ha trails the average of its group, 33.84. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its roots have white flesh. Dry matter is 32.5 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. Its cyanide level, the HCN content, is low. A low level is safer for the table, while a high level calls for peeling, soaking and full cooking. It is recommended .
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** White flesh, dry matter about 32.5 percent, low HCN.
**Where:** All regions, best in Southern Mindanao.
Moderately resistant to brown leaf spot, bacterial blight and spider mite.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a sweet, low cyanide UPLB selection from CIAT seed, released for food and feed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant CM3419 2a cassava

It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Lakan 2 (UPL Cv 6) the same as CM3419 2a?
items.a: Yes. Lakan 2 (UPL Cv 6) is another name for CM3419 2a, registered as NSIC 1995 Cv 11. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 28.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of CM3419 2a?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
